data.narrative:
Curio Solutions is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Ed McGinnis and Pete Zweifel that has raised $16M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 total entities—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Oklo—all operating in the same frontier nuclear sector at same or adjacent stages.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised ($16M) as a proxy for post-money valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for progression from Series A to the next funding round, implying $32M. Peer-median analysis draws on three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B). The median of this set is $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a low estimate of $27M, a median of $420M, and a high of $929M. The wide range reflects substantial dispersion in nuclear energy company valuations at early stages, driven by differences in technology maturity, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity assumptions. Key uncertainties include the appropriate peer weight given Valar Atomics' outlier valuation and the degree to which Curio's specific technical differentiation justifies positioning within this range.
